data.rationale: The commit addresses a bug in eval_const_expressions() where simplifying CASE, COALESCE, or NULLIF expressions to a single argument failed to preserve the original expression's collation and typmod. This occurs when CASE has a constant condition, COALESCE has a leading non-nullable argument (like a literal), or NULLIF has a constant NULL second argument. Without an explicit applyRelabelType() call, subsequent grouping or ordering operations might use the wrong collation, potentially leading to wrong results or plan-time errors. The proposed grammar fragment adds specialized alternatives to create these patterns (e.g., CASE with 'true', COALESCE with literals) combined with explicit COLLATE clauses to exercise the fix.
data.grammar_fragment: expr<T> : <0.5> CASE WHEN "true" THEN expr<T> ELSE expr<T> END ; expr<text> : <0.5> COALESCE "(" @lit(text) "," ( @lit(text) COLLATE '"C"' ) ")" | <0.5> NULLIF "(" expr<text> "," ( "NULL::text" COLLATE '"POSIX"' ) ")" ;
seeds: CREATE TABLE t_simp (c text NOT NULL); INSERT INTO t_simp VALUES ('a'), ('A'); SELECT count(*) FROM (SELECT COALESCE(c, 'x' COLLATE "C") FROM t_simp GROUP BY 1) q;
SELECT count(*) FROM (SELECT CASE WHEN true THEN c1 ELSE 'x' COLLATE "POSIX" END FROM t0 GROUP BY 1) q;
SELECT NULLIF(c1, NULL::text COLLATE "C") FROM t0 GROUP BY 1;

rewrites.name: case_true_metamorphic
rewrites.template: CASE WHEN true THEN {e} ELSE 0 END
rewrites.why: CASE with a constant TRUE condition simplifies to its branch, which must preserve its typmod and collation.

rewrites.name: nullif_null_metamorphic
rewrites.why: NULLIF with a constant NULL second argument reduces to the first argument while preserving collation metadata.
